The military convention between Bulgaria and the Central Powers laid down the general plan for Bulgaria's campaign against the Kingdom of Serbia.
The military convention severely limited the control of the Bulgarian High Command over the Bulgarian 1st Army.
The Bulgarian 1st Army was designated part of a combined German, Bulgarian and Austro-Hungarian force.
The combined force was commanded by Field Marshal August von Mackensen.
Mackensen had recently led the German and Austro-Hungarian armies in the highly successful and victorious Gorlice-Tarnów Offensive of the Central Powers against the Russian army on the Eastern Front.
Mackensen's army group was created specifically to wage war against the Serbian army in the pre-1913 borders of the country ('Old Serbia').
Mackensen's army group was created to defeat the Serbian army wherever it found it.
Mackensen's army group was created to open the land route between Hungary and Bulgaria.
As commander, Mackensen acted independently.
Mackensen received his directives only from the German High Command.
The field marshal's orders to his Bulgarian forces had to be relayed to the commander of the Bulgarian 1st Army by the Bulgarian General Staff.
The relay of orders through the Bulgarian General Staff left room for the General Staff to intervene when needed.
Under the convention, the Bulgarian commander-in-chief retained full and direct control over the Bulgarian 2nd Army.
The Bulgarian 2nd Army operated in Vardar Macedonia.
